title: Black Panther Watermelon (Black Panther F1): Characteristics
metaDescription: Black Panther watermelon is an F1 hybrid watermelon variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Black Panther watermelon is an F1 hybrid watermelon variety, also sold or known as Black Panther F1. It is not a registered variety, so the facts here come from its seller and farm sources. It comes from Allied Botanical.

heroImage.alt: Ampalaya seedlings planted through plastic mulch on raised beds, the kind of farm where Black Panther watermelon is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for Black Panther F1, this is the same watermelon. The facts below come from its seller and from farm sources, each one listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [watermelon variety finder](/crop-varieties/watermelon), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for gourds and melons](/land-preparation/cucurbit-land-preparation).
Key facts about Black Panther watermelon

blocks.caption: From its seller and farm sources
rows: Days to harvest, per the seller

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Days to harvest, by the seller's count: 60 to 65 days after transplanting. No trial on record checks this figure yet, so treat it as the seller's own and compare with farms near you before you plan a season around it.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit watermelon fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [damping off](/diseases/damping-off), [downy mildew of cucurbits](/diseases/downy-mildew). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Days to harvest:** 60 to 65 days after transplanting.
**Fruit:** Round, glossy solid dark green rind, juicy red flesh, 6 to 8 kg.
Intermediate resistance to gummy stem blight.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: in Allied Botanical's current watermelon list, the only evidence found is the company's own listing. These are the seller's own figures, from its own trials. So plant a small area first, and compare it with your usual watermelon on the same ground.
Where and when to plant Black Panther watermelon

Watermelon pays best in the dry season on sandy, well drained ground. Choose by fruit size and flesh: a sweet red flesh and a rind thick enough for the trip to market. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is Black Panther F1 the same as Black Panther?
items.a: Yes. Black Panther F1 is another name for Black Panther. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
No. It is a hybrid, so seed saved from it does not grow true and yields less. Buy new seed each season.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Black Panther?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
